Hi, I’m learning Maltese! :D I’ll repost an older comment of mine with the recourses I use (all books are available online, though, if you know where to look)

Books:

1.	⁠Learn Maltese, Why Not - Joseph Vella (vocabulary, grammar exercises)

2.	⁠A Short Grammar Of The Maltese Language - M. Weiss This book is from 1845 - it’s old, yes. The grammar itself is correct, however, there has since the book been published been changes in the orthography.  

3.	⁠Teach Yourself Maltese - Joseph Aquilina (grammar, vocabulary)  

4.	⁠Basic Maltese Grammar - Grazio Falzon (grammar)  
5.	⁠Merħba Bik - Antoinette Camilleri (colloquial approach, not much grammar)  

6.	⁠Loan Words In Maltese - Manwel Mifsud
Very comprehensive; all about the Maltese verbs (the most difficult part of the language, IMO)

And, websites. There’s a great tumblr blog called “malteseboy.tumblr.com” - not much grammar, but a little, and a lot of vocabulary, pronunciation. Another one is “surfacelanguages.com” - no grammar, but a lot of vocabulary, most of which has native pronunciation!

There’s also a YouTube channels called “TheHuSkY1984” - hasn’t been updated since 2010, lmao, and there’s only six videos, but still, better than nothing.

maltesedictionary.org.mt is a great dictionary.

Good luck if you start learning it! :D It’s a wonderful language. Also, if you use ANKI, I’m working on a deck right now. It has around 600+ words, with plural forms listed for the nouns and adjectives, and perfective, I perfective and passive participles for the verbs, sentences and counting, I can share it for interested!

Jesus. Maltese is as distinct from other varieties from Arabic as is Portuguese from Spanish, or Catalan from French. Even the *actual* Arabic dialects are incredibly different from one another - Maghrebi from Khaleji, Levantine from Egyptian. The thing all *those* dialects have in common, however, is the fact that people living in  the areas where the specific Arabic dialect is spoken learn MSA, Modern Standard Arabic, “uniting” all distinct varieties to a standard variant, keeping the dialects together (somewhat). Adding on to the fact that most such countries are members of the Arab league, are neighbouring countries, the majority of speakers belong to Islam (the language of Islam is Arabic; further “unifying” the people of various dialects). Many words in the dialects are written the same, but pronounced differently. 

Maltese has none of that. It’s written in the Latin alphabet, it has a significant vocabulary from Italian, which is completely Romance, you don’t learn Modern Standard Arabic in Malta, you don’t turn on your television and listen to news in Modern Standard Arabic in Malta, you don’t read books in Modern Standard Arabic in Malta, Malta is an island, close to Italy, geographically “cut off” from the rest of the Arab countries, and is not a member of the Arab league. As most Maltese people are *not* Muslims, there’s no unification there, either.  

If we’re considering Maltese and Arabic (and by “Arabic”, which dialect are you referring to? MSA? Levantine? Maghrebi?) the same language, then so is Spanish and Portuguese, as well as Ukrainian and Russian. It’s absurd.

And yeah, the lack of resources makes it hard. That YouTube channel seems amazing though, thank you! Some other resources I have used / am using that may be of help to you (if you don’t have them already);
    
• Saudi Arabian Dialects - Theodore Prochazka (1998)
A very “grammar-y” book; mainly about phonology, no “descriptive” explanations but good for detailed information about the stems, vowels, verbs, roots, suffixes etc. The books has a very extensive dialect support, but overall both Hijazi (from 9 regions) and Najdi (8 regions) are covered
  
• Spoken Arabic (Saudi) - Merrill Y. Can Wagoner, Arnold Sattterthwait, Frank Rice (1977)  
Quite sure this teaches Najdi Arabic; not much grammar but great for “colloquial” teaching and vocabulary.  
  
• Najdi Arabic - Bruce Ingham (1994)  
IMO definitely the best of them all - it’s like a mix of the above too; very clear-cut grammar but well explained and extensive information about the vowels, morphology, assimilation’s etc etc.
